content: The incidence of Grade 3–5 adverse events and serious adverse events (SAEs) will be assessed. Specific adverse events of interest include QT prolongation, peripheral neuropathy, optic neuritis, myelosuppression, and hepatotoxicity. Participants will be categorized based on the treatment regimen and dose they were assigned. The proportion of individuals who completed their assigned linezolid dose will also be reported. Comparisons between regimens will be conducted using risk difference or relative risk. Pharmacokinetic data on linezolid will be collected and presented when available from included trials. The WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis (Module 4: Treatment – Drug-resistant tuberculosis treatment, 2022 update) outline various regimens for multidrug-resistant or rifampin-resistant tuberculosis (MDR/RR-TB). These include: 1. WHO-recommended long all-oral regimens (18–20 months): These regimens are based on drug groups, including Group A (fluoroquinolones [Fq], bedaquiline [Bdq], linezolid [Lzd]) and Group B (cycloserine, clofazimine, and possibly Group C medicines). An example is an 18-month regimen of Bdq (≥6 months), levofloxacin/moxifloxacin (Lfx/Mfx), Lzd, and clofazimine or cycloserine. 2. WHO-recommended shorter all-oral regimens (9–11 months): These regimens include Bdq and Fq but exclude Lzd. An example is a 4–6-month regimen of Bdq (6 months), Lfx/Mfx, clofazimine, pyrazinamide (Z), ethambutol (E), high-dose isoniazid (Hh), and ethionamide (Eto), followed by a 5-month continuation phase of Lfx, clofazimine, Z, and E. 3. South African shorter all-oral regimens (SA_new): Used since 2008, these regimens include Bdq, Fq, and Lzd. An example is a 4–6-month regimen of Bdq (6 months), Lzd, Lfx, clofazimine, Z, E, and Hh, followed by a 5-month continuation phase of Lfx, clofazimine, Z, and E. 4. Experimental regimens (e.g., NExT trial): A 6–9-month regimen of Bdq, Lfx, Lzd, Z, and Eto (or high-dose isoniazid or terizidone). 5. BPaL regimens: These regimens include bedaquiline, pretomanid (Pa), and linezolid. Variations in linezolid dosing and duration are explored to reduce toxicity. Examples include: Lzd 1200 mg for 26 weeks + Pa + Bdq Lzd 1200 mg for 9 weeks + Pa + Bdq Lzd 600 mg for 26 weeks + Pa + Bdq Lzd 600 mg for 9 weeks + Pa + Bdq Lzd 600 mg for 16 weeks, then 300 mg for 8 weeks + Pa + Bdq 6. BPaLM regimens: These regimens add moxifloxacin (Mfx) to the BPaL combination. An example is a 6-month regimen of Bdq, Pa, Lzd, and Mfx. Older injectable-based regimens (e.g., kanamycin, capreomycin, amikacin) are no longer recommended by WHO. The safety and efficacy of these regimens are evaluated based on treatment success, failure and recurrence, death, loss to follow-up, adverse events (including drug-drug interactions for HIV-infected patients), and amplification of drug resistance. Data sources include clinical trials (e.g., NExT, TB-PRACTECAL, Nix, Zenix) and country-level contributions. Specific questions addressed in the guidelines include: The use of shorter all-oral regimens (<12 months) containing at least three Group A drugs for MDR/RR-TB patients without Fq resistance. The safety profile of BPaL regimens with varying linezolid exposure in MDR-TB patients. The use of 6-month regimens (e.g., BPaL, BPaLM) for pulmonary MDR/RR-TB with or without Fq resistance. The potential for modified BPaL regimens with lower linezolid exposure to replace the original BPaL regimen. The guidelines emphasize stratification by factors such as age (adults, adolescents, children), comorbidities (HIV, diabetes), smear and culture positivity, cavitation on chest X-ray, and smoking status. Statistical analyses are conducted to compare outcomes across regimens and assess the impact of modifications in treatment protocols.
